text.title: JPA / Hibernate Procedure
text.summary: 5-step procedure to apply the JPA / Hibernate methodology end-to-end.

step.name: model-entity
step.input: Domain aggregate definition, business key field
step.action: Create entity class with `@Entity` + `@Table`. Declare all associations as `FetchType.LAZY`. Implement `equals`/`hashCode` over the business key. Use `@Getter @Setter`, never `@Data`. Add audit timestamps (`@CreationTimestamp` with `updatable = false` + `@UpdateTimestamp`, or `@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)`) and `@Version` where the aggregate is user-editable. For each association write a Javadoc line justifying the cascade, `orphanRemoval` and fetch choice.
step.output: Entity class + business-key documentation + justified associations
step.decision-gate: If any association is `EAGER`, BLOCK per `lazy-by-default` rule.
If audit timestamps are missing, BLOCK per `audit-timestamps` rule.
If any association uses `CascadeType.ALL` without a written justification, BLOCK per `justified-cascade-fetch` rule.

step.name: ship-paired-migration
step.action: For every entity diff, author a Flyway migration `V<n>__<name>.sql` in the same PR. Apply expand-contract for any rename/type change. Declare foreign-key indexes and unique constraints explicitly — Hibernate does not always emit them. Set `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate` in `application-prod.yml`.
step.output: Paired migration on disk + validate mode active
step.decision-gate: If migration is missing, BLOCK per `flyway-migration-per-entity-change` rule.

step.name: add-repository-with-bulk-safety
step.action: Define a narrow repository interface listing only the operations the services actually call; back it with a Spring Data `JpaRepository` implementation interface that the services never see. Add `JpaSpecificationExecutor` only when dynamic filtering is genuinely required. For bulk updates/deletes, annotate `@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true, flushAutomatically = true)`. Use `@Query("... JOIN FETCH ...")` or `@EntityGraph` for opt-in eager loading. For read-only list endpoints define interface or class projections and return `List<XDto>` rather than entities.
step.output: Narrow repository interface with safe bulk ops + DTO projection queries
step.decision-gate: If raw `JpaRepository<T, ID>` appears in a service method signature, BLOCK per `narrow-repo-interface` rule.
If a list endpoint loads full entities for a few fields, BLOCK per `dto-projection-on-reads` rule.

step.name: add-service-with-dto-projection
step.action: Implement `@Service` methods that fetch entities and map to DTOs inside a `@Transactional` boundary — `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` on query methods, `@Transactional` on writes, never on repository methods. Controllers consume the DTO; entities MUST NOT cross the controller boundary. Catch `OptimisticLockException` on `@Version`-guarded aggregates and surface a domain error.
step.decision-gate: If controller returns an entity, BLOCK per `dto-projection-in-controllers` rule.
If a repository method carries `@Transactional`, BLOCK per `service-owns-transaction-boundary` rule.

step.name: add-datajpatest-slice
step.action: Author `@DataJpaTest` with Testcontainers (`@Container static PostgreSQLContainer ...`). Disable OSIV (`spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`) in all profiles and add a CI check that fails if the property is missing or true. Enable `hibernate.generate_statistics` in the test profile and assert the query count on list paths to catch N+1 before it ships.
step.output: Repository slice tests green + OSIV off
step.decision-gate: If repository test uses `@SpringBootTest`, fail per `datajpatest-for-repositories` rule.
